To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
service bundling is a collaborative strategy which is driven by the need of the tourism industry to overcome fragmentation.

1) the drivers of the adoption of service bundling are the need for differentiation, the search for a competitive advantage, and the need for a better control of the supply chain; 2) the drivers of collaboration differ according to the networking orientation of hoteliers; 3) the drivers of service bundling can also be used as a tool to segment the hospitality industry according four clusters, namely Relational / Social, Opportunists, Innovators, and Marketers.

1) the development of service bundles is mainly driven by relational and marketing motivations; 2) the hospitality industry shows a high degree of fragmentation, with different approaches to collaboration and different motivations to be part of a partnership.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the drivers of service bundling, and with the segmentation of the hospitality sector according to operators’ collaboration orientation.
the study of the drivers of the service bundling phenomenon, and the segmentation of the hospitality market according to the networking orientation of hoteliers.
the analysis of the networking orientation of hoteliers in order to understand the factors that influence their collaboration and the motivations for being involved in service bundling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the study has identified the different types of networking orientation of the hospitality industry and their motivations for being engaged in collaborative partnerships.
service bundling is a strategic option for tourism destinations, which should be encouraged and supported by policy makers.
the hospitality industry is a very dynamic and competitive industry and that hoteliers have to be constantly aware of new trends and opportunities in order to survive and to grow in the long term.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the study contributes to the understanding of the networking orientation of tourism operators.
service bundling represents a new form of collaboration that allows to overcome the fragmentation and the competition of the tourism industry.
the hospitality industry is not a homogeneous sector, but it consists of a variety of different players.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the development of service-bundling strategies is a complex and multifaceted process that requires a deep understanding of operators’ attitudes towards collaboration.
collaboration is not a one-size-fits-all approach.

service bundling is a promising strategy to overcome the fragmentation in the tourism industry, and that the development of service bundles is driven by the networking orientation of tourism operators.
